html:
Rock and roll is a kind of popular music that grew up in the United States in the late 1940s and 1950s, mostly in the South. It mixed rhythm and blues, gospel and country music, with a strong backbeat, electric guitar and lyrics about youth, cars and love.

Black musicians laid most of its ground. Chuck Berry, Little Richard and Fats Domino had hits that young white listeners also bought. The disc jockey Alan Freed helped popularise the name.

In 1954 Elvis Presley recorded "That's All Right" at Sun Records in Memphis, and Bill Haley's "Rock Around the Clock" soon topped charts. Radio, cheap records and the new teenage market spread the sound fast. Many adults saw it as a threat to morals and to racial segregation.

In the 1960s British bands such as the Beatles took it back to America and around the world, and "rock" grew into many forms. Rock and roll, like jazz before it, was one of the great American cultural exports of the century.
